ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, points A, B, and C are on the circle with center O. If $\angle C=20^\circ$ and $\angle B=30^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle A$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $\because$ $\angle C=20^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle O=2\angle C=40^\circ$,\\
$\because$ $\angle O+\angle A=\angle B+\angle C$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle A=30^\circ+20^\circ-40^\circ=\boxed{10^\circ}$

The radii OA and OB are drawn in the figure, and chords AC and BC are also drawn. Reasoning: It is known that ∠C=20°, and it is an inscribed angle subtending arc AB, so the corresponding central angle ∠AOB=2×20°=40°. Then trace angles along rays AC, AO, OB, and BC: the angle from AC to OB can be expressed as ∠A+∠AOB, and can also be expressed as ∠C+∠B. Therefore ∠A+40°=20°+30°, so ∠A=10°.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: A, B, and C lie on the circle; O is the center; radii OA and OB are drawn, and chords AC and BC form the marked angles. Interpret ∠A as the angle between AC and AO, ∠B as the angle between BO and BC, and ∠C as the inscribed angle ACB. From the text, ∠C=20° and ∠B=30°. Since ∠C subtends chord/arc AB, the central angle ∠AOB is twice it, so ∠AOB=40°. Then angle-chase the four rays AC, AO, OB, BC: the angle from AC to OB can be decomposed as ∠A+∠AOB, and also as ∠C+∠B. Hence ∠A+40°=20°+30°, giving ∠A=10°.
